summary: Source-reviewed rework recovered the activity/toxicity rows from XML Tables 3/4 and resolved the prior publication blocker with cautions for database nomenclature and limited mechanism depth.

per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_1_database: Linked DBAASP assay/experiment rows were rechecked against primary XML Tables 1-4. Rows with exact value/entity support are source_verified except Xav rows, where a primary-source/database target-name conflict is explicitly preserved as source_conflict.
per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_2_activity_toxicity: All Table 3/4 MIC and hemolysis cells were converted into row-level records with endpoint, raw value, unit, target, assay conditions, and primary-source locators. Primary-source-only rows are retained when the linked database snapshot has no corresponding row.
per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_3_mechanism: Mechanism output is accepted only as indirect contextual framing; no direct mechanism assay is claimed from this paper.
per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_4_publication_grade: The prior hard blockers are closed; remaining issues are nonblocking cautions and no targeted rework remains open.

caution_findings.evidence_context: Primary source footnote/methods use Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. vesicatoria 2133-2 for Xav, while linked DBAASP rows use Xanthomonas campestris pv. Vesicatoria 2133-2. MIC values are table-matched but these database rows remain source_conflict.

Worker-2 extracted all Table 3/4 peptide rows; the linked DBAASP snapshot covers a subset and sometimes condenses repeated hemolysis values, so unmatched primary-source-only rows are retained without fabricating database identifiers.

Local supplementary assets were opened by file type and packet supplementary indexes; they are HTML/indexed-only surfaces and no structured supplementary activity spreadsheet/table was locally recoverable.
Mechanism record is limited to source-located contextual background; no direct paper-local mechanism assay is promoted.
